- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast peaks.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust downward bias for extended periods of low volatility or mean reversion.
- Model tends to overreact to recent high prices, leading to overshoots; dampen momentum-driven forecasts.
- When true values show strong mean reversion (e.g., after high peaks), model fails to correct quickly; apply smoother decay toward historical mean.
- Forecast horizon matters: 30-day forecasts often overestimate if recent prices are rising; underpredict if recent prices are falling or consolidating.
- Avoid overfitting to recent data; if history shows strong downward trend, don’t assume continuation; introduce lagged momentum correction.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate; add buffer for post-spike correction.
- Model underestimates when true values are clustered near low end of range; increase baseline offset for low volatility periods.
